data.name: FLCN / FNIP1/2
data.description: Folliculin and its binding partners FNIP1/2; act as a GTPase-activating protein (GAP) for RagC/D, switching the Rag heterodimer into the configuration that recruits mTORC1 to the lysosome. FLCN-FNIP complements the GATOR1/GATOR2 arm by regulating the RagC/D half of the cycle. Loss of FLCN causes Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome through a SUBSTRATE-SPECIFIC defect rather than blanket mTORC1 hyperactivation: canonical outputs (S6K1, 4E-BP1) are largely preserved, while TFEB and TFE3 escape phosphorylation and accumulate in the nucleus (NAP2020).
data.description_beginner: A protein complex that helps switch the Rag GTPases into the right configuration to bring mTORC1 to the lysosome - working alongside, but through a different route than, the GATOR1/GATOR2 system. Losing it causes a genetic disease (Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome) not because mTORC1 goes generally haywire, but because a couple of its specific outputs (TFEB and TFE3) stop being properly turned off.

studies.title: FLCN loss is characterized by SQSTM1/p62 accumulation despite functional autophagy flux in Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome-associated kidney cancer
studies.authors: Ullern H; Johannessen JA; Kasikci F; Formica M; Karimi Melve N; Andresen S; Brech A; Axcrona K; Jørgensen K; Farkas L; Enserink JM; Knævelsrud H

evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: BHD patient-derived kidney cancer cell line; Norwegian BHD patient tumor cohort
studies.finding: In BHD patient-derived kidney cancer cells, FLCN loss causes constitutive nuclear TFEB localization and mTORC1 hyperactivation, but leaves bulk autophagy flux and LC3 lipidation unaffected; however, the autophagy receptor SQSTM1/p62 accumulates in enlarged puncta, a finding replicated in a Norwegian cohort of BHD patient kidney tumors, showing p62 accumulation is dissociable from bulk autophagic flux.

studies.model_system: Human cell lines; ATP6V1B2-mutant follicular lymphoma patient samples
studies.finding: Identifies a nutrient-independent lysosomal pathway in which v-ATPase recruits TBK1/ULK1 to phosphorylate FNIP1, inhibiting the FLCN:FNIP complex and releasing TFEB for nuclear translocation; recurrent ATP6V1B2 mutations found in follicular lymphoma patients constitutively hyperactivate this axis, driving TFEB-dependent tumor proliferation.

studies.title: Synergistic role of TFEB/TFE3 and mTORC1 in kidney cystogenesis and tumorigenesis
studies.authors: Ferniani M; Sambri I; Huynh T; Pennella R; Tufano G; Herz NJ; Rossi B; Iannaccone A; Trepiccione F; Calcagnì A; Ballabio A

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Kidney-specific conditional knockout mice: Depdc5-KO, RagC-KO, and Flcn/RagC double-KO (models of Birt-Hogg-Dube and Tuberous Sclerosis Complex)
studies.finding: Using kidney-specific mouse models that genetically uncouple mTORC1 activity from TFEB/TFE3 activity (Depdc5-KO, RagC-KO, and Flcn/RagC double-KO), the authors show mTORC1 hyperactivation -- not TFEB/TFE3 activation alone -- is the primary driver of kidney cystogenesis and tumorigenesis in Birt-Hogg-Dube and Tuberous Sclerosis Complex models. Constitutive TFEB/TFE3 activity further accelerates disease on top of mTORC1-driven pathology.

studies.title: Substrate-selective mTORC1 regulation and gene dosage-dependent tissue divergence in Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome
studies.authors: Cao ZL; Zhao SC; Lin F; Liu YH; Hong XT; Hong LY; Xu LQ; Li FP; Yu HY; Yao WG; Chen WY

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Narrative synthesis (human genetics + mouse mechanistic data)
studies.finding: Reframes Birt-Hogg-Dube (BHD) syndrome beyond the classic 'global mTORC1 hyperactivation' model: FLCN acts as a GAP for RagC/D, giving substrate-selective (not global) mTORC1 control. Biallelic FLCN loss drives kidney tumors via MiT/TFE nuclear accumulation, while haploinsufficiency alone is sufficient for lung and skin lesions -- resolving the 'mTORC1 paradox' via gene dosage and signaling timing. Narrative synthesis of human genetics and mouse mechanistic data.

studies.title: Structure of the lysosomal mTORC1-TFEB-Rag-Ragulator megacomplex
studies.authors: Cui Z; Napolitano G; de Araujo MEG; Esposito A; Monfregola J; Huber LA; Ballabio A; Hurley JH

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: First structural view of how mTORC1 actually reaches TFEB to phosphorylate it: two full Rag-Ragulator complexes present a single TFEB molecule to the mTOR active site, one in the normal Raptor-docking arrangement and a second, non-canonical one that grips TFEB's own first helix. Mutating that grip point drives TFEB straight into the nucleus (turning on autophagy/lysosome genes) without disturbing where mTORC1 itself sits. Explains, at the level of atoms, why TFEB phosphorylation needs the tumour suppressor FLCN and the GDP-loaded state of RagC in a way no other mTORC1 substrate does. Boundary: cryo-EM of a complex reconstituted from purified human proteins — a static structural snapshot, not a live cell or a real-time measurement.

relations.mechanism: FLCN-FNIP is the GAP for the other half of the Rag dimer (RagC/D). Only when both halves are in the right nucleotide state can the dimer hold mTORC1. Crucially this arm is SUBSTRATE-SPECIFIC: it gates TFEB and TFE3 phosphorylation, while canonical outputs like S6K1 and 4E-BP1 carry on without it.
relations.mechanism_beginner: FLCN flips the other half of the Rag pair into its working shape – but it only changes one specific output (TFEB), not the whole pathway.
relations.boundary: The substrate selectivity is why Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome is driven by constitutive nuclear TFEB/TFE3 rather than by blanket mTORC1 hyperactivation (NAP2020).

relations.mechanism: When lysosomes are stressed, ULK1 (or its relative TBK1) phosphorylates FNIP1 at S296 on the lysosome. This switches the FLCN-FNIP complex off, so mTORC1 can no longer hold TFEB in the cytoplasm and TFEB moves into the nucleus.
relations.mechanism_beginner: ULK1 tags FNIP1, which turns FLCN off and lets TFEB escape mTORC1's grip.
relations.boundary: Human cell lines and ATP6V1B2-mutant follicular lymphoma samples; a nutrient-independent lysosomal-stress route, and TBK1 can substitute for ULK1. Single study.
